title: Jimmy Noone, Tiny Parham and cabaret life at the Dreamland
summary: He worked briefly with Noone's small fake band; cabarets had floor shows, cover charges and owner Bill Bottoms.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: What was Noone's band like, at Dreamland?
Now, that band I didn't work with.
Which band did you work with, with Jimmy?
I'm trying to think now. Am I supposed to be on that band at Dreamland?
Well, I don't know.
(Unintelligible)
Well, I have here, the Apex, and then I think when I talked to you a few weeks ago you mentioned the Dreamland. Did you work --
I worked with Tiny Parham at the Dreamland.
Did you work with Jimmy Noone?
Yeah. But I didn't -- I wasn't with him very long at the Dreamland.
Uh-huh. Did he have a big band or a small band?
It was a small band.
Yeah? Do you remember who was in it?
No, I don't. The one I remember is the drummer, Zutty Singleton.
Uh-huh. Was it a fake band or a reading band?
Yeah.
Fake band?
Fake band.
At the Dreamland, did people dance there, or --
It was a cabaret.
And people danced in all the cabarets?
Yeah. And you had a little, small show.
Well, that was during Prohibition. Were they like speakeasies, or was whisky served?
Uh-huh -- no, you had to bring your own whisky and get your own set-up.
I see. What did the club do, just provide the band and --
The show.
Did they charge to get in?
Band and show. No, you had a cover. What they called a cover charge. Small cover charge, but it was just like admission.
Sure. Did they do good business?
Yeah, fine business.
All those places?
All those places did business.
Were they operated by the gangsters, or --
No, the Dreamland was operated by one man.
Who was he?
Bill Bottoms.
Bill Bottoms. Was he a white man
or black man?
Black man.
There was more than one Dreamland, weren't there two Dreamlands?
Yeah, well, that was the Dreamland Ballroom. That was on West Side.
That was different?
Yeah, that was different. See, that was a long time ago, and that was a ballroom, Dreamland Ballroom, where Charlie Cook had the band.
Did you ever work with Charlie Cook?
No.
